Resolves #21915

Tear the Scheduler and Gantt out of a gallery opening plan. Drag **Focus lighting** a day later in the Scheduler and watch its Gantt bar, its Board dates and the dependent **Sound check** move. Drag it to another person's row to hand the work over. Closing the pop-ups returns the same components to the dock.

![Three browser windows after moving Focus lighting to Noor](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/656de994dd1b834344a53a0c5063e6f882cc6cd1/review-evidence/21915/composite.png?raw=true)

Run `examples/dashboard/planning/index.html` on a local Engine server. On a phone, the Board opens first and all three views are available as tabs.

Evidence: L3 (two physical Chromium drags, two native pop-outs and returns, three distinct browser windows and one shared App Worker) → L3 required.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| 1 · Opening and docking | The opening names one task to drag. The real dock controls move the resident Scheduler and Gantt into two new windows. Closing each popup returns its pane. |
| 2 · Shared identity | [Browser and App Worker receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/656de994dd1b834344a53a0c5063e6f882cc6cd1/review-evidence/21915/receipt.json) records three CDP windows, their Neo window IDs, one App Worker, and identical references across views. |
| 3 · Visible dates and resource rows | A physical drag moves Focus lighting from Nov 11–13 to Nov 12–14 UTC (exclusive end). Gantt geometry and the card's dates update in the other windows. A second drag moves the visible booking from Mara to Noor. Collapsing the installation phase only hides those tasks in the Gantt. |
| 4 · One scheduling writer and return | The existing Gantt scheduling operation moves Sound check from Nov 13–16 to Nov 14–17. Print labels stays on its original dates. Each date edit fires once. Returning the pop-ups restores the original component IDs and the same task object. |
| 5 · Replay and pictures | `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/SharedPlanning.spec.mjs` replays the gestures. [Board](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/656de994dd1b834344a53a0c5063e6f882cc6cd1/review-evidence/21915/board.png), [Scheduler](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/656de994dd1b834344a53a0c5063e6f882cc6cd1/review-evidence/21915/scheduler.png) and [Gantt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/656de994dd1b834344a53a0c5063e6f882cc6cd1/review-evidence/21915/gantt.png) are separate browser-content captures of the same session shown above. |

## Deltas from ticket

Includes the shared store prerequisite from #21919. A new lazily created `TaskStore#getBookingStore()` exposes the same leaf records to the Scheduler and Board while letting the booking view filter independently of the tree. Two-argument Gantt range reads still follow tree expansion. [Store contract, tests and measured cost](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21919#contract-ledger). The existing Workstation planning desk keeps its independent release plan.

- The candidate Portal showed the card once in each of its five groups. The real theme switch selected both covers and a normal click opened all three views. [Browser test and prepublication routing details](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21915#issuecomment-7084767150).
- Six Chromium journeys passed across `SharedPlanning` and `DockTearOutDefaultRoute`. Both phone themes, shared selection, date and resource edits, return identity, refused invalid dates and selection after a tab change are covered. An additional browser check followed the opener's dark/light switch in both detached windows.

The bundled App, Data and VDom workers loaded and all three planning widgets rendered with their production CSS. The examples-body and file-size checks passed.
- Integration head `6c8187e26d` brings in merged Board and Provider changes. All six Chromium gestures and phone/tear-out tests passed again, alongside 384 focused unit tests. On the preceding head the three new tests also passed in [hosted Chromium](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/45063109613/job/137333306070). Frame critique: the three views fit in the 960 × 540 opening with four people and eight tasks visible. A short timeline bar can abbreviate a title, which the tree and selected Board card give in full. After the drag, **Sound check** occupies Nov 14–16 inclusive and overlaps Noor’s **Walk the floor** on Nov 16. The Scheduler draws both bookings in half-height lanes. We kept this conflict visible so a visitor can see the resource consequence of delaying the predecessor.

# PR Review Summary

**Status:** Request Changes

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Request Changes
- **Rationale**: No §0 catalog row fires. The code and the store contract are merge-ready. The three actions below touch only evidence and the body, so no code has to change. This isn't Approve because the 📸 rendered-surface gate is Required-Action tier. It isn't Approve+Follow-Up either: evidence for this PR's own surface can't move to a later ticket.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Thanks, Emmy. The ownership split is right: the TaskStore owns identity and membership, and the view borrows the same records. The view gets its own Model, so record changes still go to the canonical store. The Scheduler routes its edits through the Gantt's writer with the same `fields` merge as `Gantt#commitTimelineEdit`, and the gesture spec counts each change, so "once" is measured.

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #21915 (ACs), #21919 (Contract Ledger), and these dev sources: `src/gantt/TaskStore.mjs` (two-argument visible-row `getRangeRecords`), `src/timeline/store/Events.mjs` (resource-aware static range), `src/timeline/Column.mjs:1005` and `src/scheduler/Container.mjs#getResourceEvents` (both pass `resourceId` to a custom store's range method), and `src/data/TreeStore.mjs#splice` (hidden-branch fallback `mutate`). Also [Clio's design read](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21915#issuecomment-7078958863) and the sibling `examples/dashboard/tearOut/Viewport.mjs`.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** The TaskStore owns a flat `timeline.store.Events` view of its structural leaves, holding the same record instances. Structural writes reconcile the view and visibility changes don't, and the view is destroyed with the store. `getRangeRecords` keeps its two-argument contract and sends an explicit resource to the view. The demo borrows the provider's stores, sends Scheduler date edits through the Gantt writer, and the engine hardcodes no demo ids. For isolation, each unit test owns and destroys its store, and the e2e cleans up windows and witnesses in `finally`.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `getBookingStore()` clones the Model, so `RecordFactory#onRecordChange` still resolves `Neo.get(model.storeId)` to the TaskStore, which forwards `recordChange`, `rowsChange` and `updateKey`. Writes under a collapsed phase arrive through TreeStore's fallback `mutate`, and silent writes through the `splice` override's version check. Collapse runs through `Collection#splice` and fails the `differs` test. The Gantt paints inline rows (it sets no `eventStore`), so the new resource branch can't reach it. Re-keying edits the view's maps directly because `Collection#updateKey` reads the item's key, which the canonical store has already changed, so its no-op guard would skip the update. Justified.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. #21919 measured the wrong-resource and collapse defects in a real App Worker before prescribing a fix. The PR proves identity with receipts (CDP window ids, one worker target, per-record change counts) rather than prose. Body-only work; no Brain surface.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: Three watch items, none blocking. (1) `getBookingStore()` returns one view per TaskStore. Its filters are independent of the tree but shared by every borrower, so a Board filter would also hide those bookings from the Scheduler. The guide's "has its own filters" is accurate, but one clause would stop a reader assuming per-consumer filters. (2) `onBookingMutation` walks the whole structure after every structural write and every silent splice, so the cost grows with the plan, not the change. The ledger measured 0.62 ms at 2,000 leaves. A 100k plan loaded in silent batches would pay that walk on every batch. *Hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation.* (3) The single-writer route is an example override of `moveEvent`, so every app that shares a booking view with a Scheduler copies it. An engine seam, such as a Scheduler config naming the writer, would retire it. *Hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation; no ticket minted, none found open.*
- **Falsifier run:** a leaf that gains a child through a move (`store.add({id:'b', parentId:'a'})`), with the phase expanded and collapsed. Result: 2/2 green. The control `getChildren('a')` returned `['b']`, the view dropped `a`, and the resource `'1'` range read returned `[]`. I deleted the temporary spec afterwards.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: A store that borrows another store's records needs its own Model instance. `RecordFactory#onRecordChange` routes through `model.storeId`, so sharing the Model would hand change ownership to the borrower. `getBookingStore()` is now the reference for this.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: The stock landing camera times out on SharedWorker apps, so the covers needed an independent capture. That is tracked in #22010 and fixed by #22014.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The reconciliation covers every TreeStore write path: the fallback `mutate` for collapsed branches, the `splice` override for silent writes, a `mutate` listener ordered `before` so observers registered earlier still see settled membership, and the `isLeaf` flip on ingest when a leaf gains a child.
